# 07. Content Strategy

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Ensure the site says the right things, in the right order, with credible proof and maintainable content structures.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A content model for each page type with required fields, optional fields, proof needs, CTA, metadata, and owner.
- [ ] A message hierarchy for homepage, service pages, portfolio pages, articles, location pages, and contact pages.
- [ ] A proof plan mapping claims to evidence such as examples, metrics, testimonials, credentials, photos, or process details.
- [ ] A terminology guide for service names, industries, locations, audience labels, product names, and forbidden wording.
- [ ] A readability standard for headings, body copy, lists, captions, buttons, form labels, and legal summaries.
- [ ] An editorial calendar or content backlog for static blog and evergreen pages.
- [ ] A content freshness policy for dates, prices, team members, testimonials, case studies, offers, hours, and compliance content.
- [ ] A source-of-truth policy for facts, data, quotes, certifications, legal claims, and regulated statements.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Every page must have unique value; no page may exist only to target a keyword or location with near-duplicate text.
- [ ] Headings must communicate the argument of the page when scanned without body copy.
- [ ] Content must answer user objections before asking for high-commitment actions.
- [ ] The most important information must appear before decorative storytelling.
- [ ] Claims must be precise enough to be meaningful and modest enough to be defensible.
- [ ] Content must remain accurate when shared in search snippets, social previews, and browser tabs.
- [ ] Long-form content must include structure that supports scanning, jumping, and returning.
- [ ] Translated content must be localized for meaning, proof, units, dates, currency, and legal expectations.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check every page for outdated dates, unsupported superlatives, duplicated sections, empty claims, and missing next steps.
- [ ] Check that CTAs use clear action language and match the user's readiness.
- [ ] Check that title tags, meta descriptions, H1s, and page intros tell a consistent story.
- [ ] Check that testimonials and case studies include permission, context, and no misleading edits.
- [ ] Check that portfolio entries state role, constraints, process, output, and outcome where possible.
- [ ] Check that contact and form copy sets expectations for response time, privacy, and required information.
- [ ] Check that legal and compliance content is reviewed by qualified counsel where the business risk requires it.
- [ ] Check that content owners can update static files or source content without breaking markup.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid lorem ipsum, placeholder testimonials, generic AI copy, empty adjectives, and unsupported guarantees.
- [ ] Avoid keyword stuffing, doorway pages, hidden text, and repeated city-swap content.
- [ ] Avoid writing only for search engines or only for stakeholders.
- [ ] Avoid vague CTA labels such as submit, learn more, or click here when a specific action is available.
- [ ] Avoid publishing regulated claims without legal review.
- [ ] Avoid content that depends on images alone to communicate essential facts.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The copy must make the business easier to choose, not just easier to describe.
- [ ] Every important claim must have visible proof nearby or a credible path to proof.
- [ ] Content must be useful when printed, shared, indexed, translated, or read by assistive technology.
- [ ] The content system must support ongoing publishing without losing quality control.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use audits to flag duplicate titles, missing descriptions, empty headings, broken internal links, thin pages, and missing image alternatives.
- [ ] Use content reports as review prompts; do not let automation approve claim quality.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Copy clarity: direct sentences, short paragraphs, meaningful headings, useful subheadings, benefits tied to needs, plain-language features, specific claims, and human tone.
- [ ] Scanability: headings expose key points, bullets/cards separate ideas, long blocks are avoided, visual rhythm guides reading, CTAs stand out, and mobile text remains readable.
- [ ] Tone is consistent with audience and brand, avoids random shifts, exaggeration, empty cliches, unsupported claims, jargon without context, and language that disrespects user intelligence.
- [ ] Content accuracy covers business name, services/products, contact details, prices, locations, dates, team names, legal info, partner names, certifications, claims, terminology, and no placeholders.
- [ ] Blog, portfolio, case study, product, multilingual, legal, FAQ, testimonial, and metadata content follow their own quality rules and are maintained after launch.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
